## Why this is not wiring

`WriteWavePublisher` (`crates/engine/src/rotation/rotate_write.rs`) is the write-plane rotation's transport edge. #1014 landed the two read-plane seams over the real network plane and deliberately stopped short of this one: three of its five methods are plumbing, but `republish` cannot be implemented against the seam as it stands.

Both blocking questions are now answered by **[ADR 0004 — Read-body child names are rewritten by the write-plane name wave](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0004-read-body-child-names-on-the-name-wave.md)** (FSM1/cipher-box-next#58, merged). **Read it before starting** — it settles a second, larger gap that this issue originally did not name.

## What the ADR settles

**D1 — the publisher re-resolves; it is not handed the authoring material.** The record handed to `republish` carries only routing identity:

```rust
pub struct RepublishedNode {
    pub node_id: [u8; 16],
    pub new_name: IpnsName,
    pub write_epoch: u64,
    pub is_root: bool,
}
```

Authoring at `new_name` additionally needs the node's read body, the read key it seals under, and the predecessor name. Widening this struct does not work as stated, because the orchestrator does not hold that material either — `WriteScopeNode` is `{node_id, current_name, child_node_ids}` — so it would mean widening `WriteSubtreeResolver` too, and dragging O(subtree) bodies and per-node key material through a primitive that currently holds exactly one secret.

Instead: add **`current_name: IpnsName`** to `RepublishedNode`, and let the concrete publisher do the gated read at `current_name` and author at `new_name`. This mirrors the landed read-plane precedent — `OwnerRotationNet::publish_scope_root` already does exactly this, and says so in code: *"The read body and the envelope fields a republish preserves come from the node's own current record, gated — the rotation carries neither."* The resume contract stays trivially intact: `is_republished(new_name)` is unchanged and still answers from published state alone.

**D2 — the read body cannot be carried verbatim.** `ChildRef.ipns_name` (`crates/core/src/seal/body.rs`) lives in the **read** body. The wave moves every node in the subtree to a freshly derived name, so afterwards every parent's child refs name nodes that have moved, and once interior old names batch-retire they name nothing.

Write-grantees are fine — they derive names from `writeScopeSeed`. **Read-only survivors cannot**: `open_grant_blob` returns `write_scope_seed: None` for a read-only grant, and the re-point object carries `currentRootName` and no other name. So without a rewrite, a read-only grantee reaches the new root and cannot descend. #26 D3's "read-only survivors follow republished mirrors" was pointing at exactly this and was never elaborated; the blueprint dropped the clause entirely.

So the wave **rewrites each `ChildRef.ipnsName`** to the child's freshly derived name and re-seals the read body under the node's unchanged read key at the unchanged read epoch. Child-first ordering already makes every child's new name known before its parent publishes.

## Scope

1. **Widen `RepublishedNode` with `current_name`** and update `rotate_scope_write`'s call site plus the simulation tests.
2. **Land the concrete `WriteWavePublisher`** over `RecordTransport` + `ApiClient`:

   - `is_republished` over the fan-out GET;
   - `republish` over the gated read at `current_name`, the read-body child-name rewrite, then `net::author` + `net::record_publish`, signing under `kdf::ipns_keypair(write_seed(freshWriteScopeSeed, node_id))`;
   - `publish_repoint` across the three channels — scope pointer, mailbox, old-root tombstone.
3. **Thread the read-plane material the rewrite needs** — the node's read key, and a nonce from the entropy seam. The read epoch must **not** move: a same-epoch rewrite is not a read rotation and must raise no read-epoch floor (#38 D1, each plane's clock authored by its own authority).

- [ ] ADR 0004 `Status:` flipped to `Accepted — implemented in FSM1/cipher-box#<this PR> (merged)` via a follow-up commit on cipher-box-next, per the ADR 0002 precedent

- After a wave, a read-only holder starting from the re-pointed `currentRootName` resolves **every** node in the subtree — asserted at depth greater than one, so a root-only pass cannot satisfy it.

## Problem

`WriteWaveNet::publish_scope_pointer` (`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:1349`) publishes the scope pointer through `publish_inline` and then advances the sequence floor. The pointer therefore dies at its 90-day client-signed EOL. The API republisher is keyless by design and cannot extend a client-signed validity, so nothing renews it.

The scope pointer is the **canonical** re-point channel. `publish_repoint` (`net/rotation.rs:1487`) returns `NotLanded` for both `RepointChannel::Mailbox` and `RepointChannel::Tombstone`, so the pointer is currently the only landed channel a read-only survivor has.

`HeldRecord.head_cid` (`liveness.rs:63`) is a required `/ipfs/` head, and a held record with an empty head CID is skipped at `liveness.rs:245`. The pointer's `Value` is the sealed block inline, not a head CID. So the held-set shape cannot carry an inline record as it stands.

Give `HeldRecord` an inline-or-head value shape, and enrol the scope pointer at publish time. Keep the release-active empty-head guard for the head variant.

2. Each row's tag must bind at the **old** name, which is what catches a swapped `recipientEncPk`.

4. The re-minted `pseudonymPk` must equal the committed one — it binds the scope, not the name, and it authorizes structure signing.
5. `expires_at` and `unknown` carried forward on both the entry and the ledger row.
6. Sorted by tag, not by the order a write-grantee authored.

One poisoned row now aborts the write wave and the read cascade, which are exactly the rotations that cut the attacker. #1127 specifies fail-closed and that is what shipped, but the availability trade was never weighed when the issue was written.

The victim stays locked out across the owner's rotation. That fix belongs in `crates/core`.
- `sweep_pass` is reached from `create_read_grant`, which **does** hold the owner subkey, so the same descendants get checked on one leg and unchecked on the other. Noted in #1143 rather than widened in this PR.

Three correctness defects on the prune path, all in `crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs`.

## \#849 — a root-only retire orphans every sealed leaf

`plan_prune` emitted root content CIDs only, but `POST /registry/retire` deletes rows for exactly the CIDs handed to it and never interprets content — it is zero-knowledge and cannot expand a root. Retiring a version therefore dropped the root's pin row and left every sealed leaf pinned and charged forever, while `reclaimed_bytes` reported the whole version freed. At the frozen 1 MiB framing any file over one chunk has more leaf bytes than root bytes, so this was the normal case.

New `expand_retire_targets(version, root_block)`. The root block is plaintext deterministic CBOR, so the leaf list is readable by CID alone with no key and no wire-format change.

- **Fail-closed throughout.** The block is refused past `MAX_RESOLVED_RECORD_BYTES` before it is hashed, then verified against the version's `contentCid` through `decode_content_cid_str` + `is_plane_anchor` + `verify_cid` — the same spelling `read.rs` and `staging.rs` already use, so the trust failure carries core's `TrustViolation::ContentCidMismatch` and an off-plane root CID is refused as malformed rather than conflated with a substituted block.
- **The walk is one level.** `decode_root` already enforces that every link is a `raw`-codec CID, and a raw block names no further links.
- **Leaves first, root last.** The root block is the only record of its own leaf list, so retiring it first would make those leaves unnameable and charged forever — exactly the defect, made permanent instead of transient. A drain that dies mid-expansion can always re-expand from a root that is still pinned.

`plan_prune` still emits roots only; the expansion is the drain-time step, matching the ledger-stores-roots decision in \#872. The API needed no change: the existing `retire` already takes an advisory lock on every path, bulk-deletes via `In(targets)`, and refcounts before unpinning, which is exactly right once the client hands it the full set.

`ContentVersion.size_bytes` was documented as the pinned size but was fed from `Version.size`, which is plaintext. Sealing adds 40 B per leaf plus the root block, and pinned bytes are what the registry charges, so the figure understated every reclaim and every quota pre-flight.

## The gap

Sealed bytes exceed plaintext by a fixed, computable amount:

- 40 B per leaf — a 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce plus a 16-byte tag (`crates/engine/src/content/chunk.rs:65,93`)
- plus the DAG root block itself: 41 B fixed + 38 B per inlined leaf CID

At the #820-frozen framing (`chunk_size = 1_048_536`, sealed leaf exactly 1 MiB) that is 78 B per chunk, so the under-report is small in ratio but always present and always in the same direction: **`reclaimed_bytes` understates what is actually freed**, on top of the much larger overstatement from the root-only retire defect. The two errors are independent and point opposite ways, so neither masks the other reliably.

The same conflation reaches the quota pre-flight: #822 §5 ruled the pre-flight must be sized in **sealed** bytes, because sealed bytes are what `registerPin` charges (`apps/api/src/content/content.service.ts:275`). Quoting plaintext under-reports every time.

## Fix

Pick one unit per field and make the conversion explicit at the boundary rather than implicit in an assignment. Derive the pinned total from the leaf count and root size rather than reusing the plaintext number, and add a test asserting `reclaimed_bytes` equals the sum of the sizes the retire call actually frees.

########## 872 ##########
engine: prune old versions and reclaim their bytes
---
Prune drops old file versions and reclaims their bytes. Prune is a **write-plane mutation** — it re-seals and publishes a shortened history — which is why #820 pulled it into this chain. Slice settled by #825 on wayfinder map #813.

## Scope

**This issue absorbs #849, #850 and #851 outright.** They were previously named as prerequisites in prose only, with no dependency edge, which made #872 look startable when it is not — and made three defects look like three shippable PRs. They are not: `plan_prune` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:93`) has **zero production callers** at `main` @ `3d087d673`. Its only references are the re-exports at `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:54` and `crates/engine/src/content/mod.rs:38`, and its own unit tests in `retention.rs`. Nothing reaches it, so none of the three is independently observable or independently testable end-to-end. Close all three as folded-in when this ships. Native `blocked_by` edges are recorded on this issue so the graph stays honest until they are.

**Three correctness fixes, folded in.**

- **#849 — leaf expansion.** `plan_prune` emits root content CIDs only, and `POST /registry/retire` deletes rows for exactly the CIDs handed to it without walking the DAG, so every sealed leaf stays pinned and charged forever while `reclaimed_bytes` reports the whole version freed. Expand each doomed root to `root + leaf_cids` before retiring, by fetching the root block and `decode_root`-ing it — the root block is plaintext det-CBOR, so no key is needed. Two constraints on its shape: `root + leaf_cids` **cannot be one call** — the registry batch cap is `REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX = 1000` (`crates/engine/src/net/mod.rs:25`), enforced by the chunking at `crates/engine/src/net/retire.rs:100`, and a 1 GiB version is 1025 targets at the frozen 1 MiB framing, so partial retire is normal at exactly `max_file_bytes` — and **leaves retire before their root**.
- **#850 — unit mismatch.** `ContentVersion.size_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:75`) is documented as the **pinned** size, but the prune path fills it from `Version.size`, which is **plaintext** bytes. The gap is fixed and computable (40 B per sealed leaf, plus the root block). A pending-reclaim total built on the wrong unit is the same misreport in a new place. Derive the pinned total from the leaf count and root size rather than reusing the plaintext number.
- **#851 — partially already fixed; check before you write.** The ticket claimed `keep_latest` admits zero at `retention.rs:72-73`. That is stale in two ways. `RetentionPolicy::KeepLatest(NonZeroU64)` **already exists** (`crates/engine/src/content/retention.rs:65`), with the doc stating the zero state is unrepresentable rather than guarded. The hole survives only on the free function: `plan_prune(versions_newest_first: &[ContentVersion], keep_latest: usize)` at `retention.rs:93` still takes a plain `usize` and `skip(0)` still yields the whole history including the live version. Close that one signature; do not re-do the enum.

**One op that ends at publish, plus a retire ledger that is not an op** (#852). Both alternatives put a garbage-collection call on the critical path of user work: one op with two legs holds the FIFO head so the next rename waits on cleanup, and two ops repeats that plus a sixth `OpKind` with vacuous rebase semantics.

**The ledger stores roots; leaves are re-derived** at drain time via `decode_root` — plaintext det-CBOR, no key. That is three orders of magnitude smaller, and it is the irrecoverable half: once the publish lands nothing readable references the dropped roots, while leaves always can be recovered from a root.

**Leaves before root, versions oldest-first.** The journaled root **is** the expansion key, so retiring it first makes its leaf list unnameable and those bytes charged forever. Oldest-first is what `plan_prune` already emits — `PrunePlan.retire_targets` is documented "oldest first" (`content/retention.rs:82`) and the plan is built by iterating the doomed suffix in reverse (`content/retention.rs:99-103`) — and it leaves a valid suffix of history. Together these make the drain resumable across restart with nothing journaled but roots.

**Entries clear only on the server's own done-signal** — a batch reporting `retired: 0`, which is positive evidence and also covers the succeeded-but-response-lost case. Everything else backs off forever: **no attempt budget, no gave-up list, no dead-letter class.** Every failure is either self-clearing (offline, 401, a 429 from the registry throttle, a 503 from lock contention) or ours (a 400 from a bad CID we emitted, an unfetchable root we are charging for), and in every case the only user action is `Command::ManualRefresh`, which already exists.

**Owed bytes ride the entry** as one `u64` from `ContentVersion.size_bytes` — in the corrected pinned unit, per the folded-in #850 — and surface as a **vault-level pending-reclaim figure** beside the quota, the ticket's own missing "record of what was owed".

**Mode-derived legs, bytes tracking hosted.** Hosted to hosted, External to provider, Dual to both; the byte figure drains on hosted confirmation. External accounts hold **size-zero rows** (`register()` records membership at size 0, hosted ingress refused for BYO, `content.service.ts:246-253`), so a hosted-only ledger would self-satisfy instantly in External mode.

**A distinct `RetireLedger` seam** with its own conformance kit, on `FloorStore`'s precedent. It diverges from the op queue on lifetime, ordering (a set, not a FIFO), failure contract (never-discard versus dead-letter) and cancellability at once. Reusing the op queue is cheaper and inherits #832's owner tag free, but it puts a non-FIFO non-cancellable record in a store whose cold-start sweep **deletes** what it cannot decode.

**Owner-scoping is forced, not tidy.** Account A's owed CIDs retried under account B's token delete no rows, return `retired: 0`, and satisfy the done-signal without reclaiming anything.

## Harvest reference

`apps/api/src/ipfs/pending-unpin/` on branch `v1` is the same shape server-side: a durable outbox drained in ordered batches, per-row failure isolation ("leave row for next run; do not abort the batch"), a refcount-then-unpin helper, and a depth gauge. v1 could place it server-side only because it called Kubo `pin/ls` directly; v2 cannot, since no endpoint lists an account's pin rows (#826).

## Acceptance

- `plan_prune` cannot be called with a zero keep-count — unrepresentable, not guarded.
- `reclaimed_bytes` equals the sum of the sizes the retire call actually frees, in pinned bytes.
- A pruned 1 GiB version retires across multiple `REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX` batches, leaves before root, and is resumable after a mid-drain restart.
- A retire returning `retired: 0` clears the entry; every other failure retries.
- The pending-reclaim figure drains to zero on hosted confirmation and never on an External-only leg.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`, `Contract Suite`.

## Problem

The vault settings **write** plane is fully built and reachable from nothing. `publish_settings` (`crates/engine/src/settings.rs:464`) has no production caller — its only references are the re-export at `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:92`, its own `#[cfg(test)]` module, and the `crates/engine/tests/vault_settings.rs` suite. `Command` has seventeen variants and none of them is a settings command.

The **read** half is already wired: `load_settings` is called at `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1643` inside `Engine::start`, and it already refuses a lapsed record.

The slice that authored the write plane, #870, is closed. No open issue picks the caller up. #643 promises a settings view "over the facade" while no facade command exists, and it is gated behind #635 and #642 in any case.

## Why it matters

A settings record is what carries the account's placement decision. Until a caller exists, no account can ever change its placement away from the cold-start default, and every hardening already landed on this plane — the EOL check from #904, the revision check from #928 — guards a path no user can reach.

It also hides a cliff. `load_settings` is live and fails closed on a lapsed record, so the day a publish caller lands without renewal beside it, the 90-day EOL in #1043 becomes a real availability defect rather than a latent one.

## Scope

- Add the settings command arm to the facade, so a host can write the vault settings record.
- Enrol the published name in the held set in the same change, so `eol_renew_pass` (`crates/engine/src/net/liveness.rs:219`) covers it — this is #1043, which cannot be built before this issue decides the key.
- Thread the command through `crates/wasm/src/host.rs` and `packages/client` so a host can actually call it.

## The held-set key is this issue's decision

`HeldRecords` is `BTreeMap<[u8; 16], HeldRecord>` (`crates/engine/src/net/liveness.rs:91`), keyed by **node id**. The settings record has no node id. Every existing insert comes from `net/resolve.rs:369`, `net/resolve.rs:597`, or `sync/drain.rs:2057`, all of which do have one. So #1043's proposed one-line insert does not type-check as written, and the key is a decision this slice must make, not a detail #1043 can settle on its own.

## Gate

`Engine Tests`. Note that the EOL renewal itself is only reachable under the injected virtual clock — no e2e tier advances wall time, so `crates/engine/tests/vault_settings.rs` is the ceiling for the renewal half.
